text:
Summary:
This LessWrong post introduces “activation engineering”, a technique that steers an already-trained language model by adding carefully-chosen activation vectors during the forward pass. It shows that a single “truthfulness” steering vector, built as the difference of truthful vs. untruthful activation patterns, doubles GPT-2-XL’s TruthfulQA score, and suggests further research directions such as PCA-derived steering vectors.  

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[87]  
Inference strategy justification: All explicit causal statements were captured; whenever a pathway element (e.g. PCA-based steering) lacked empirical results, a low-confidence validation node was created and flagged, satisfying the “all categories” rule while keeping inference clearly marked.  
Extraction completeness: Every claim that links the core risk (untruthful answers) to the proposed steering interventions is represented, and all nodes are connected in one fabric.  
Key limitations: 1) The source is a short blog post, so many links rest on qualitative statements—edge confidence is therefore often medium or low. 2) Some open-problem suggestions have no published data; corresponding validation nodes are speculative.  
Prompt-improvement note: Allow “prospective validation” as an explicit validation-evidence subtype for open-problem proposals; this would make confidence tagging clearer.
